world.title: Egypt’s Military Delegation Meets Defence Minister Fiqi in Mogadishu
world.description: MOGADISHU — Somalia’s Minister of Defence, Ahmed Moallim Fiqi, received a delegation of Egyptian military officers at his office on Saturday, accompanied by Egypt’s Ambassador to Somalia, Mohamed Salah Keshtah. The meeting focused on strengthening relations and cooperation between the two nations, with both sides exchanging views on matters of mutual interest and the advancement of collaboration in the defence and security sectors. Minister Fiqi commended the Egyptian government’s support for safeguarding Somalia’s sovereignty and unity, as well as its backing of Somalia’s efforts to combat terrorism and rebuild the Somali National Army. Background of the Partnership The defence relationship has deepened steadily over the past two years. Ambassador Keshtah, who was appointed to his post in late 2025, has been actively engaged with Somali officials across multiple sectors, as detailed in FTL Somalia’s reporting on Somalia-Egypt strategic ties. Security and defence cooperation have emerged as central pillars of the relationship, with Ambassador Keshtah previously holding talks with Minister Fiqi on advancing defence sector collaboration. In August 2025, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi signed a defence agreement described by the Somali president as a “testament to a future of common defence against international terrorism.” Egypt has since contributed military weapons and equipment to Somalia as part of efforts to bolster the Somali National Army’s operational capacity. Egypt’s role in the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) has also progressed. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty confirmed that Egyptian troops will be stationed in the Middle Shabelle region, where they will work closely with the Somali National Army to strengthen local capacity and ensure civilian protection. President El-Sisi confirmed in February 2026 that arrangements for the deployment of Egyptian forces were in progress. business.title: Diagnostic performance of a 4-miRNA blood panel for colorectal cancer
business.description: Early detection of colorectal cancer (CRC) significantly improves clinical outcomes; however, the widely used faecal immunochemical test (FIT) exhibits suboptimal sensitivity. We aimed to develop a blood-based diagnostic panel using high-mannose (HM)-associated miRNAs captured by recombinant Oscillatoria agardhii agglutinin (OAA1). Using a two-stage design, we analysed retrospective discovery (n = 99) and prospective validation (n = 21) cohorts. Serum HM-associated miRNAs were captured using OAA1-immobilised columns and quantified by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Multivariate logistic regression identified an optimised 4-miRNA panel (miR-122-5p, miR-130a-3p, miR-15b-5p, and miR-126-3p) with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.886 in the discovery cohort. The panel score exhibited a significant stage-dependent increasing trend across the adenoma–carcinoma sequence (P < 0.0001) and showed no significant association with tumour location, maximum tumour diameter, or conventional tumour markers. In the independent validation cohort, this panel achieved an AUC of 0.944, with 100% sensitivity and 83.33% specificity. These results suggest that the OAA1-captured 4-miRNA panel can serve as a non-invasive liquid biopsy tool for early CRC detection. This may help address the anatomical and tumour-burden limitations of the FIT, supporting the panel’s potential utility as a secondary screening strategy in clinical practice.

business.title: Joint entropy-aware quantization for energy-efficient TinyML human activity recognition on IoT edge devices
business.description: Sensor-based human activity recognition (HAR) is a core task in wearable healthcare, assisted living, sports monitoring, rehabilitation, and context-aware Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems. However, deploying HAR models on microcontroller-class edge devices remains challenging because continuous inference must satisfy strict constraints on Flash memory, SRAM usage, latency, and energy consumption. Conventional TinyML-HAR pipelines commonly rely on uniform INT8 or INT4 quantization, which reduces computational cost but assumes that all sensor channels, neural layers, activations, and activity windows require the same numerical precision. This assumption is suboptimal because wearable motion signals exhibit heterogeneous information content: static activities often produce low-entropy inertial patterns, whereas dynamic and transitional activities generate richer and more quantization-sensitive signal distributions. To address this limitation, this paper proposes JEAQ-HAR, a joint entropy-aware quantization framework for energy-efficient TinyML HAR on IoT edge devices. JEAQ-HAR estimates entropy at the sensor-channel, neural-layer, activation, and input-window levels to guide a hierarchical mixed-precision allocation policy across the HAR inference pipeline. High-entropy sensor axes, quantization-sensitive layers, and complex motion windows are assigned higher precision, while low-entropy and redundant components are quantized more aggressively. The framework also introduces an entropy-distortion regularization objective to preserve activation-distribution structure during quantization-aware training and an adaptive inference policy that selects low-bit or higher-precision execution paths according to window-level motion complexity. Experiments on UCI-HAR, WISDM, and PAMAP2 show that JEAQ-HAR achieves macro-F1 scores of 95.1%, 93.1%, and 90.1%, respectively, with an average gap of only 0.47 percentage points from the FP32 backbone. Across the three datasets, the average serialized deployment package size is reduced from 159.6 KB for FP32 to 29.17 KB for JEAQ-HAR, corresponding to an 81.7% reduction relative to the FP32 serialized package, rather than merely the raw trainable-weight tensor. On microcontroller-class devices, JEAQ-HAR reduces the complete measured end-to-end inference latency and energy from 14.0 ms and 1.07 mJ for FP32 to 5.93 ms and 0.47 mJ, including entropy computation, routing, packed-precision handling, quantized inference, and decision generation. These gains represent end-to-end workload reductions rather than speedups from native INT6 arithmetic. Compared with uniform INT4 quantization, JEAQ-HAR improves average macro-F1 by 4.8 percentage points while maintaining a compact memory footprint and low inference cost. The ablation study confirms that sensor-level entropy, layer-level entropy, window-level entropy, entropy-distortion regularization, and adaptive inference each contribute to recognition stability or deployment efficiency. These results show that combining entropy-guided precision allocation with deployment-aware TinyML evaluation provides an effective and practical strategy for accurate, compact, and energy-efficient HAR on constrained IoT edge devices.
